# AI Security for Builders — Exercise Sheets

Work in tables of 3–4. Each lab ends with something written down that you take back to work.

## Lab 1 — Threat model your system

*Module 1: Threat model · about 48 minutes*

**With demo 1** (`python demos/01_threat_model.py`): Draw your system as boxes and arrows. For every arrow that carries untrusted text, name the threat and the control. No control = your backlog.

**Write down:** 1) what you tried · 2) what the result was · 3) one thing you will do differently at work this month.

## Lab 2 — Implement 5 controls

*Module 2: Controls · about 72 minutes*

**With demo 2** (`python demos/02_implement_five_controls.py`): Implement the five controls in your own stack. Re-run your attack list after each. Which attack needs TWO controls?

**Write down:** 1) what you tried · 2) what the result was · 3) one thing you will do differently at work this month.

## Lab 3 — Red-team exercise

*Module 3: Red-teaming · about 48 minutes*

**With demo 3** (`python demos/03_red_team_exercise.py`): Add five attacks specific to your domain (your tools, your data). Run the probe weekly. Track 'attack success rate' as a metric, like test coverage.

**Write down:** 1) what you tried · 2) what the result was · 3) one thing you will do differently at work this month.

## Lab 4 — Governance hooks

*Module 4: Governance hooks · about 24 minutes*

**With demo 4** (`python demos/04_security_gates_and_metrics.py`): Map these checkpoints onto your own release process. Which gate has no security evidence today?

**Write down:** 1) what you tried · 2) what the result was · 3) one thing you will do differently at work this month.
